question: Why is material wealth insufficient compared to possessing the kaula knowledge?
premises: One may possess vast accumulated wealth.
Even an ocean filled with jewels is imaginable.
Such wealth is contrasted with the teaching.
inference: Even immense material wealth is not comparable to the value of this kaula knowledge.
uncertainties: ratnasaṃpūrṇamakretuṃ is a difficult fused form; interpretation is tentative.
plain_english: Even if one had an accumulation enough to fill the ocean with jewels...
